concepts.title: Indus Valley or Harappan Civilisation Overview
concepts.definition: The Harappan Civilisation flourished in the Indus valley from about 2600 BCE to 1900 BCE, making it one of the earliest urban civilizations of the world.
concepts.key_idea: The Harappan Civilisation was a Bronze Age urban culture spread across north-western India and present-day Pakistan, known for its planned cities.
question_patterns: calculate the duration of the Harappan civilisation
describe the time period of the Indus Valley civilisation
name the major sites of the Harappan civilisation
why is it called the Harappan civilisation
explain the significance of the Indus Valley civilisation

solution_steps.explain: Note the mature phase from about 2600 BCE to 1900 BCE.
Subtract the end year from the start year to find how long the mature civilisation lasted.
A duration of about 700 years shows the civilisation was long-lived and stable.

worked_examples.question: Calculate the duration of the mature Harappan Civilisation from 2600 BCE to 1900 BCE.
worked_examples.solution: duration = 2600 - 1900 = 700 years.

worked_examples.question: Name two major sites of the Harappan Civilisation.
worked_examples.solution: Harappa and Mohenjo-daro were two major cities of the civilisation.

worked_examples.question: Why is the civilisation called Harappan?
worked_examples.solution: It is named after Harappa, the first site of this civilisation to be discovered.

exercises.question: State the time period of the Harappan Civilisation and calculate its duration.
Name three major sites of the Indus Valley Civilisation.
Explain why the Harappan Civilisation is considered one of the earliest urban civilizations.

concepts.title: Town Planning and Drainage
concepts.definition: Harappan cities were carefully planned with a grid of streets, rectangular houses of baked bricks, and an advanced covered drainage system.
concepts.key_idea: The systematic town planning and drainage of Harappan cities show a high level of civic organisation and engineering skill.
question_patterns: describe the town planning of Harappan cities
explain the drainage system of the Indus Valley civilisation
what materials were used to build Harappan houses
how were the streets of Harappan cities arranged
why is Harappan town planning considered advanced

solution_steps.explain: Streets were laid out in a grid pattern, crossing each other at right angles and dividing the city into blocks.
Houses were built of baked bricks, usually with a courtyard, wells, and bathrooms, showing concern for hygiene.
Confirm that covered drains ran along the streets, connected to house drains, with soak pits and manholes for maintenance.

worked_examples.question: How were the streets of Harappan cities arranged?
worked_examples.solution: Streets were laid in a grid pattern, intersecting at right angles.
worked_examples.answer: In a grid pattern at right angles

worked_examples.question: What material was mainly used for Harappan houses?
worked_examples.solution: Baked bricks were the main building material for houses.

worked_examples.question: Describe one feature of the Harappan drainage system.
worked_examples.solution: Drains were covered and connected to house drains, with manholes for cleaning.

exercises.question: Describe the town planning of Harappan cities.
Explain the drainage system of the Indus Valley Civilisation.
Discuss how Harappan town planning reflects civic organisation.

concepts.title: The Great Bath and Granaries
concepts.definition: The Great Bath of Mohenjo-daro was a large waterproof tank probably used for ritual bathing, while granaries were large storehouses for surplus grain.
concepts.key_idea: Public structures like the Great Bath and granaries reveal the importance of religion, hygiene, and food storage in Harappan society.
question_patterns: describe the Great Bath of Mohenjo-daro
what was the purpose of the Great Bath
explain the function of Harappan granaries
where was the Great Bath located
what do public buildings tell us about Harappan society

solution_steps.explain: The Great Bath was a large rectangular tank lined with bricks and sealed with bitumen, with steps leading into it.
Granaries were large brick structures used to store surplus grain, indicating organised agriculture and food management.
Confirm that these public structures point to communal activities, ritual bathing, and centralised storage of resources.

worked_examples.question: Where is the Great Bath located?
worked_examples.solution: The Great Bath is located in the citadel area of Mohenjo-daro.

worked_examples.question: What was the likely purpose of the Great Bath?
worked_examples.solution: It was probably used for ritual bathing and religious ceremonies.

worked_examples.question: What did the granaries store?
worked_examples.solution: Granaries stored surplus grain produced by Harappan agriculture.

exercises.question: Describe the Great Bath and its likely purpose.
Explain the function of granaries in Harappan cities.
Discuss what public buildings reveal about Harappan society.

concepts.title: Agriculture and Trade
concepts.definition: The Harappans practised agriculture along the fertile Indus floodplains and carried out extensive trade with regions within and beyond the subcontinent.
concepts.key_idea: Surplus agricultural production supported urban life and enabled the Harappans to trade goods such as beads, cotton, and metals over long distances.
question_patterns: describe the agriculture of the Harappan civilisation
what goods did the Harappans trade
explain the trade links of the Harappans with other regions
how did agriculture support Harappan cities
what evidence shows that the Harappans engaged in trade

solution_steps.explain: Harappans grew wheat, barley, peas, sesame, and cotton on the fertile Indus plains, using floodwaters and simple irrigation.
They traded beads, cotton, pottery, and metals with regions in India and with Mesopotamia, using land and sea routes.

solution_steps.action: Verify the link between the two
solution_steps.explain: Confirm that agricultural surplus made urban life and long-distance trade possible, supporting the prosperity of Harappan cities.

worked_examples.question: Name two crops grown by the Harappans.
worked_examples.solution: Wheat and barley were major crops grown by the Harappans.

worked_examples.question: With which civilisation did the Harappans trade?
worked_examples.solution: The Harappans traded with Mesopotamia, as shown by Harappan seals found there.

worked_examples.question: What evidence shows Harappan trade?
worked_examples.solution: Harappan seals, beads, and pottery found in Mesopotamia and other regions show trade links.

exercises.question: Describe the agriculture of the Harappan Civilisation.
Explain the trade activities of the Harappans.
Discuss how agriculture and trade supported Harappan urban life.

concepts.title: Arts and Crafts
concepts.definition: The Harappans were skilled artisans who produced beads, pottery, jewellery, metal tools, and figurines, showing advanced craft techniques.
concepts.key_idea: Specialised crafts such as bead-making, pottery, and metalworking reflect a prosperous and technologically skilled Harappan society.
question_patterns: describe the arts and crafts of the Harappan civilisation
what types of pottery were made by the Harappans
explain the bead-making industry of the Harappans
what metals were used by Harappan craftsmen
how do crafts reflect Harappan prosperity

solution_steps.explain: List crafts such as bead-making, pottery, jewellery, metal casting, and terracotta figurines.
Harappans used wheel-turned pottery, drilled carnelian beads, and worked with copper, bronze, gold, and silver.
Confirm that specialised crafts indicate a prosperous society with trade, surplus wealth, and skilled labour.

worked_examples.question: Name two crafts practised by the Harappans.
worked_examples.solution: Bead-making and pottery were important Harappan crafts.

worked_examples.question: Which metals did the Harappans use?
worked_examples.solution: The Harappans used copper, bronze, gold, and silver.

worked_examples.question: What was special about Harappan pottery?
worked_examples.solution: Harappan pottery was wheel-turned, well-baked, and often painted with geometric and animal designs.

exercises.question: Describe the arts and crafts of the Harappan Civilisation.
Explain the bead-making industry of the Harappans.
Discuss how crafts reflect the prosperity of Harappan society.

concepts.title: Seals and Writing
concepts.definition: Harappan seals, usually made of steatite, carry engravings of animals and a script that has not yet been fully deciphered.
concepts.key_idea: The seals were likely used for trade and identification, and the undeciphered script points to a literate Harappan society.
question_patterns: describe the seals of the Harappan civilisation
what material were Harappan seals usually made of
explain the significance of the Harappan script
why has the Harappan script not been deciphered
what animals are depicted on Harappan seals

solution_steps.explain: Seals were small, square or rectangular pieces, usually of steatite, engraved with animals and pictographic signs.
The Harappan script has about 400 signs and is pictographic, but it has not been deciphered because no bilingual text has been found.
Confirm that seals were probably used to mark goods for trade and as amulets, showing organised commerce and literacy.

worked_examples.question: What material were Harappan seals usually made of?
worked_examples.solution: Harappan seals were usually made of steatite, a soft stone.

worked_examples.question: Why has the Harappan script not been deciphered?
worked_examples.solution: The script has not been deciphered because no bilingual inscription, like the Rosetta Stone, has been found.

worked_examples.question: Which animal is commonly shown on Harappan seals?
worked_examples.solution: The unicorn or one-horned animal is commonly depicted on Harappan seals.

exercises.question: Describe the seals of the Harappan Civilisation.
Explain why the Harappan script remains undeciphered.
Discuss the significance of seals and writing in Harappan trade.

concepts.title: Decline of the Harappan Civilisation
concepts.definition: The Harappan Civilisation declined around 1900 BCE, possibly due to a combination of climate change, drying of rivers, floods, and a decline in trade.
concepts.key_idea: The decline of the Harappan cities was gradual and may have resulted from environmental changes and economic factors rather than a single invasion.
question_patterns: explain the possible causes of the decline of the Harappan civilisation
when did the Harappan civilisation decline
what role did rivers play in the decline of Harappan cities
how did climate change affect the Harappan civilisation
was invasion the main cause of the decline of Harappan cities

solution_steps.explain: Consider factors such as the drying of the Ghaggar-Hakra river, floods, deforestation, and changing rainfall patterns.
A decline in trade with Mesopotamia and loss of agricultural surplus weakened the urban economy.

solution_steps.action: Verify the gradual nature of decline
solution_steps.explain: Confirm that the decline was gradual, with cities being abandoned over time, rather than caused by a single sudden invasion.

worked_examples.question: Around when did the Harappan Civilisation decline?
worked_examples.solution: The civilisation declined around 1900 BCE.

worked_examples.question: Name one environmental cause of the decline.
worked_examples.solution: The drying of rivers such as the Ghaggar-Hakra contributed to the decline.

worked_examples.question: Was invasion the main cause of the decline?
worked_examples.solution: Most scholars now believe environmental and economic factors, not invasion, caused the gradual decline.

exercises.question: Explain the possible causes of the decline of the Harappan Civilisation.
State when and how the Harappan cities declined.
Discuss whether environmental or human factors caused the decline of the Harappan Civilisation.

concepts.title: Legacy of the Harappan Civilisation
concepts.definition: The Harappan Civilisation left a lasting legacy in town planning, crafts, agricultural practices, and cultural traditions that influenced later Indian civilization.
concepts.key_idea: Many elements of Harappan culture, such as planned settlements, craft traditions, and symbols, continued in later periods of Indian history.
question_patterns: describe the legacy of the Harappan civilisation
how did Harappan town planning influence later settlements
which Harappan traditions continued in later Indian culture
what can modern society learn from the Harappan civilisation
explain the importance of remembering the Harappan legacy

solution_steps.explain: Note elements like planned towns, drainage, bead-making, pottery styles, and agricultural practices that persisted in later periods.
Some symbols and practices, such as the worship of trees and mother goddesses, may have continued into later Indian traditions.
Confirm that the Harappan legacy forms an important foundation of the long continuity of Indian civilization.

worked_examples.question: Name one Harappan tradition that continued in later India.
worked_examples.solution: The worship of trees and plants appears to have continued in later Indian culture.

worked_examples.question: How did Harappan town planning influence later settlements?
worked_examples.solution: Ideas of planned streets and drainage can be seen in later Indian towns.

worked_examples.question: What can we learn from the Harappan Civilisation?
worked_examples.solution: We can learn the value of urban planning, hygiene, and sustainable use of resources.

exercises.question: Describe the legacy of the Harappan Civilisation.
Give two examples of Harappan traditions that continued in later India.
Discuss the importance of the Harappan legacy for modern Indian civilization.
